pages.title: Usage
pages.description: Install waft and run its copy, list, info, and validate commands.
pages.body:
`waft` copies selected ignored files from one Git worktree to another. Use it
for local configuration, caches, and tool state that you need in more than one
worktree but do not want to commit.

## Installation

`waft` is not published to crates.io. Install a reviewed commit from Git:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/plx/waft \
  --rev REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA --locked waft
```

Set `REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA` to the full commit SHA. Keep `--rev` in managed
environments.

## Quick start

1. Add `.worktreeinclude` to the source worktree:

   ```text
   .env
   *.env.local
   ```

2. From a linked worktree, preview the copy:

   ```sh
   waft copy --dry-run
   ```

3. Review the plan, then copy:

   ```sh
   waft copy
   ```

When run from a linked worktree, `waft` uses the main worktree as the source
and the current worktree as the destination. Pass both paths to override that
resolution:

```sh
waft copy --source /path/to/main --dest /path/to/linked
```

## Commands

| Command               | Description                                       |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `waft` / `waft copy`  | Copy eligible files. This is the default command. |
| `waft list`           | List eligible files without copying.              |
| `waft info <PATH>...` | Show detailed status for specific files.          |
| `waft validate`       | Check `.worktreeinclude` and Git ignore syntax.   |

## Global options

| Option                                          | Description                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--source <PATH>`                               | Source, usually the main worktree path.                     |
| `--dest <PATH>`                                 | Destination, usually the linked worktree path.              |
| `-C <PATH>`                                     | Operate as if started in `PATH`.                            |
| `-q, --quiet`                                   | Suppress non-error output.                                  |
| `-v, --verbose`                                 | Increase output verbosity.                                  |
| `--copy-strategy <auto\|simple-copy\|cow-copy>` | Select plain-copy or copy-on-write behavior.                |
| `--isolated`                                    | Omit user config and `WAFT_*` policy environment variables. |

## Copy options

| Option          | Description                                                  |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `-n, --dry-run` | Show what would be done without copying.                     |
| `--overwrite`   | Compatibility flag; fails on existing destination conflicts. |

## Inspect selection

```sh
waft list
waft info .env
waft validate
```

`list` prints eligible files. `info` explains why specific paths are selected
or skipped. `validate` checks rule files without copying.

## Optional post-checkout hook

Install the repository's post-checkout hook from a reviewed source checkout:

```sh
just install-hooks
```

The installer builds `waft`, copies the binary and hook into the repository's
common Git directory, and configures an absolute `core.hooksPath`. The hook
uses the pinned binary with `--isolated`; source-project configuration still
applies. The installer refuses symlinked prior hooks and worktree-specific
hook overrides.

Reinstall the hook after upgrading `waft`. Remove it and restore the previous
hook configuration with:

```sh
just uninstall-hooks
```

Do not point `core.hooksPath` at the tracked `hooks/` directory. A checked-out
branch can replace that directory before Git runs the hook.

pages.title: .worktreeinclude
pages.body:
`.worktreeinclude` patterns use `.gitignore` syntax. They select ignored files
for `waft` to copy.

```text
# Include environment files
.env
*.env.local

# Include all secret keys recursively
**/*.key

# Exclude this test key
!test.key
```

## Eligibility

A file is eligible for copying only when all of these are true:

1. It exists in the source worktree.
2. It is a regular file, not a symlink, directory, or special file.
3. It is selected by the active compatibility profile.
4. Git confirms it is ignored and untracked.
5. It is not removed by a built-in or configured exclusion.

## Profile-dependent matching

The default `claude` profile reads only the repository root
`.worktreeinclude`. The `git` profile composes nested `.worktreeinclude` files
like nested `.gitignore` files. The `wt` profile starts with every ignored,
untracked file and applies worktrunk-compatible exclusions.

Select a profile with:

```sh
waft copy --compat-profile git
```

See [Profiles](../profiles/) for the full behavior matrix.

## Validation

`waft validate` parses `.worktreeinclude` and Git ignore files and reports
syntax errors. It does not copy files.

pages.title: Safety
pages.description: Understand planning, conflicts, symlink handling, and hook trust boundaries.
pages.body:
`waft` separates read-only planning from file publication. Only `copy`
without `--dry-run` publishes files.

## Guarantees

- **Tracked files are not overwritten.** Tracked status is checked during
  planning and again under Git's index lock before publication.
- **Existing paths are not replaced.** Publication uses no-clobber semantics,
  including when `--overwrite` is supplied.
- **Symlink traversal is blocked on Unix.** Source and destination components
  are opened relative to canonical worktree directory handles with
  `O_NOFOLLOW`.
- **Publication is atomic.** Contents are synced to a temporary file before
  publication. Parent directories are synced on Unix.
- **Dry runs are mutation-free.** `waft copy --dry-run` reads and reports only.

## Concurrent changes

Normal Git writers honor the index lock and cannot change trackedness across
the final check and publication. Direct index edits that ignore Git's lock
protocol are outside this guarantee.

On Unix, directory handles prevent symlink or name swaps from redirecting a
write. Another process can still relocate an already-open destination
directory after final revalidation. Avoid concurrent destination directory
moves when pathname stability matters.

`waft` reacquires the index lock for each published file. The cost scales with
the number of selected files and index size. Keep automatic manifests narrow,
especially in monorepos.

## Hook trust boundary

Install the optional post-checkout hook only from a reviewed revision.
`just install-hooks` copies the hook and a pinned `waft` binary into Git's
common metadata directory and configures an absolute hook path. It rejects
symlinked prior hooks and worktree-specific hook overrides.

The hook runs its pinned binary with `--isolated`. Ambient `WAFT`, user config,
and `WAFT_*` policy variables cannot change automatic execution or selection.
Source-project configuration still applies.

Do not set `core.hooksPath` to a directory inside a checked-out worktree.
Branches can replace tracked hook content before Git invokes it.

## Secrets remain secrets

Every selected file becomes another filesystem copy. Backup software,
indexers, local agents, and anyone who can read the linked worktree may see it.
Use secret injection or short-lived credentials for high-value secrets.

## Preview before writing

```sh
waft copy --dry-run
```

Review the selected files and the reason for each decision.

## Overwrite behavior

Existing destination paths are always preserved. `--overwrite` is accepted for
command-line compatibility but still fails on a conflict. Review and remove a
conflicting path explicitly before copying:

```sh
rm path/to/reviewed-conflict
waft copy
```

`waft` does not remove the conflict.

pages.title: Profiles
pages.description: Choose claude, git, or wt file-selection behavior.
pages.body:
`--compat-profile` sets the missing-file behavior, matcher, rule-file symlink policy, and built-in exclusions together.
Profile Missing .worktreeinclude Matcher semantics Symlinked rule files Tool-state excludes
claude nothing selected claude-2026-04 follow none
git nothing selected git ignore none
wt every git-ignored untracked file selected wt-0.39 follow tooling-v1
## `claude` `claude` is the default. It reads only the repository root `.worktreeinclude` and matches the observed Claude Code behavior identified by `claude-2026-04`. ```sh waft copy --compat-profile claude ``` ## `git` `git` applies per-directory exclude semantics. Patterns are relative to the directory containing the rule file, and deeper rule files override shallower ones. ```sh waft copy --compat-profile git ``` ## `wt` `wt` matches the observed behavior identified by `wt-0.39`. It starts with every ignored, untracked file and removes paths matched by literal-name negations. ```sh waft copy --compat-profile wt ```

pages.title: Configuration
pages.description: Set file-selection and copy policy through config, environment, or CLI options.
pages.body:
`waft` applies configuration in the following order. Later scalar values
override earlier values.

1. Built-in defaults.
2. User config: `~/.config/waft/config.toml`.
3. Project configs: each `.waft.toml` in the resolved source worktree, from
   its repo root down to the invocation directory's equivalent source path.
4. Environment variables using the `WAFT_*` prefix.
5. CLI flags.

`exclude.extra` arrays append across layers. Set
`exclude.replace_extra = true` or pass `--replace-extra-excludes` to discard
values from earlier layers.

Project configs must be regular files. Symlinked configs fail closed, and
discovery stops at nested repositories and registered submodules.

Selecting a profile resets its four settings at that layer. Explicit settings
in the same or a later layer can override it.

`--isolated` omits user configuration, `WAFT_CONFIG_PATH`, and `WAFT_*` policy
environment variables. Built-in defaults, source-project configuration, CLI
overrides, and operational Git backend selection still apply.

## Example `.waft.toml`

```toml
version = 1

[compat]
profile = "git"

[exclude]
extra = ["*.bak"]

[copy]
strategy = "auto"
```

## CLI overrides

| Option                                                       | Description                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--compat-profile <claude\|git\|wt>`                         | Set the four profile-owned options.                       |
| `--when-missing-worktreeinclude <blank\|all-ignored>`        | Set behavior when no `.worktreeinclude` exists.           |
| `--worktreeinclude-semantics <claude-2026-04\|git\|wt-0.39>` | Select the matcher.                                       |
| `--worktreeinclude-symlink-policy <follow\|ignore\|error>`   | Set handling for symlinked rule files.                    |
| `--builtin-exclude-set <none\|tooling-v1>`                   | Select a built-in exclusion set.                          |
| `--extra-exclude <GLOB>`                                     | Add an exclusion. Repeat the option to add more than one. |
| `--replace-extra-excludes`                                   | Discard exclusions inherited from earlier layers.         |
| `--copy-strategy <auto\|simple-copy\|cow-copy>`              | Select plain-copy or copy-on-write behavior.              |
| `--config <PATH>`                                            | Replace user-config discovery with the specified file.    |
| `--isolated`                                                 | Omit user config and policy environment variables.        |

pages.title: Architecture
pages.description: How waft resolves policy, selects files, and publishes copies.
pages.body:
Each command resolves worktree context and policy, classifies files, and stops
at the last phase it needs.

## Git is authoritative

The `GitBackend` trait supplies final ignored and tracked status. `waft` does
not infer either status from `.gitignore` parsing alone.

- `GitGix` is the default in-process backend built on the `gix` crate.
- `GitCli` runs Git commands. Select it with `WAFT_GIT_BACKEND=cli`.

Backend parity tests keep both implementations aligned.

## `.worktreeinclude` matching is pluggable

`worktreeinclude_engine` applies `.worktreeinclude` rules independently of the
Git backend. It provides three matchers:

- `claude-2026-04`, the default root-rule-file behavior.
- `git`, Git-style per-directory exclude semantics.
- `wt-0.39`, worktrunk-compatible subtractive behavior.

## Command pipeline

The pipeline is read-only through copy planning.

1. Parse CLI arguments.
2. Resolve source and destination worktree context.
3. Resolve layered policy against that source worktree.
4. Validate ignore files.
5. Select candidate files.
6. Apply policy filters.
7. Confirm ignored status through Git.
8. Build a copy plan.
9. For `copy` without `--dry-run`, verify planned state and publish each file
   without replacing an existing pathname.

`validate` stops after rule parsing. `list` and `info` stop after
classification. `copy --dry-run` stops after planning.

## Testing strategy

Tests cover pure policy and matching logic, real Git repositories, each
profile, backend parity, and differential checks against Git for `git`
semantics.
